⟦m0⟧0 · How to read this manual

This manual is generated from the toolkit's own tables, so it matches the code exactly: the identifier table src/iut_ids.c (also docs/IDENTIFIERS.md, htdocs/identifiers.js, lean/IUT/Identifiers.lean), the process registry src/iut_proc.c (docs/PROCESSES.md), the C headers src/iut.h and src/iut_i.h, the diagrams of htdocs/diagrams.js and the ten progressions of htdocs/processes.js. Each entry of Part I shows one data type or notation in three ways:

  • form — the C struct that implements it, field by field, with the meaning of each field (the JavaScript model in htdocs/iut.js and the Lean port in lean/IUT/ mirror the same fields; where a Lean structure of the same name exists it is named);
  • reference — where the object is introduced or recalled in the papers, resolved to the paper, the section, the statement and the page of the PDF in pdf/, e.g. [IUT I] §3, Definition 3.1 p. 61. Papers are abbreviated as in the source code: [AbsTopIII], [Alien], [CanLift], [EssLgc], [EtTh], [ExpEst], [FormIUT], [FrdI], [FrdII], [IUT I], [IUT II], [IUT III], [IUT IV], [Pano] (see the table below);
  • identifier — the English-letters-only name (^[A-Za-z]+$, unique case-insensitively) under which it appears in the C code, the JSON, the web app and Lean, obtained from the notation through the symbol dictionary of §1.

Part II shows the processes: the ten illustrated progressions of the web app, step by step with a diagram for every step, and then all 73 processes of the registry with the transcript of iut run <id> on the demo Θ-data. Part III is a demo session: generation and validation of the Θ-data and a walk through the log-theta-lattice with the text views of the C program. The appendix is an alphabetical index of all identifiers with page numbers.

The program models the combinatorics and the numbers of the theory — which labels, which copies are identified, which indeterminacies are incurred, which inequality results — not the anabelian reconstruction algorithms; see docs/DATA_MODEL.md §8 for what is and is not computed.

⟦m31⟧Part I
The data types

347 objects in 9 chapters, grouped by kind and ordered by the paper and statement that introduce them. An entry with a form block is implemented by a C struct of its own; the others are fields, kinds or labelled instances of a struct named in the entry.

⟦m32⟧2 · Initial Θ-data, fields, places and quantities

The input of the whole theory is a collection of initial Θ-data ([IUTchI] Def 3.1): a number field F with an elliptic curve, the tower F_mod ⊆ F ⊆ K = F(E[l]) ⊆ F̄, the prime l, the orbicurve C_K, the set of places V ≅ V_mod and the odd bad places V^bad_mod. The toolkit manufactures it from an abc triple through the Frey curve, records the degrees as upper bounds and the five non-numeric hypotheses as asserted flags, and computes from it the quantities log q, |log q|, log f, log d that the final inequality is about.

54 entries: 14 data, 8 fields, 14 sets of places, 7 constants, 11 quantities.

⟦m87⟧3 · Label sets, labels, symmetries and capsules

Every Hodge theater is indexed by labels: F_l = {−l*,…,l*} for the additive F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of the Θ±ell-side, F_l^* = {1,…,l*} for the multiplicative F_l^*-symmetry of the ΘNF-side, |F_l| = F_l/{±1} in between. Capsules are finite collections of prime-strips indexed by these sets; LabCusp and LabCusp± are the torsors of cusp labels that the anabelian side reconstructs.

26 entries: 8 label sets, 7 labels, 6 symmetries, 5 capsules.

⟦m174⟧5 · Monoids, morphisms, categories, Frobenioids and maps

The Frobenius-like side: the local monoids O▷ = O× × O▶, O×μ = O×/Oμ at each v, the pseudo-monoids M^⊛ of global rational functions with the Kummer-ready / Kummer-blind distinction, the poly-morphisms (collections of morphisms, full when every isomorphism is included), the base categories D_v, D^⊛, D^⊚± and the Frobenioids F̲_v, C_v, C⊢_v, C^Θ_v, C⊩_mod, F^⊛ with the maps ρ_v, φ, χ, ζ between them.

⟦m249⟧6 · Prime-strips

A prime-strip is a collection of local data indexed by v ∈ V ([IUTchI] Fig I1.2). The nine kinds form a forgetful ladder from the holomorphic Frobenius-like F-prime-strip down to the mono-analytic étale-like D⊢-prime-strip; which rungs are preserved by the log-link (vertical coricity) and by the Θ-link (horizontal coricity) is the content of [IUTchIII] Thm 1.5. The labelled strips F_⊞, D_⊚±, F_>, F_⊛, F⊩_Δ, F⊩_LGP, … are the targets of the bridges and the homes of the pilots.

25 entries: 25 prime-strips.

⟦m275⟧7 · Hodge theaters, bridges and the gluing

A Θ±ell NF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Def 6.13) is a Θ±ell-Hodge theater (capsule F_T, Θ±-bridge to F_⊞, Θell-bridge to D_⊚±) glued along 0, ⊞ ↦ > to a ΘNF-Hodge theater (capsule F_J, Θ-bridge to F_>, NF-bridge to F_⊛), which contains the Θ-Hodge theater of Def 3.6 carrying q̲_v and Θ̲_v. Every vertex • of the log-theta-lattice is one such theater in its own universe.

23 entries: 12 Hodge theaters, 10 bridges, 1 gluings.

⟦m299⟧8 · Links, the log-theta-lattice, log-shells and pilots

The vertical arrows of the lattice are log-links (fresh Frobenius-like monoids, shared étale-like data, log-shells I_v = (p*)⁻¹ log(O×) in the codomain); the horizontal arrows are Θ-links in their Θ, Θ×μ, Θ×μ_gau, Θ×μ_LGP, Θ×μ_lgp flavours, gluing the Θ-pilot {q̲^{j²}} of † to the q-pilot {q̲} of ‡ while identifying only G_v and O×μ. The two sides of a Θ-link are mutually alien copies; the proof uses only the infinite H of columns 0 and 1.

21 entries: 9 links, 5 lattices, 5 log-shells, 2 pilot objects.

⟦m321⟧9 · Indeterminacies, the multiradial representation, structures and properties

What survives the passage across the Θ-link: processions S^±_{j+1} of tensor packets of log-shells, the splitting monoids of the LGP-monoids and copies of F_mod^×, all up to the indeterminacies Ind1 (automorphisms of processions of D⊢-prime-strips), Ind2 (Ism on O×μ) and Ind3 (upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence) — the multiradial representation of [IUTchIII] Thm 3.11, whose log-volume gives Cor 3.12.

⟦m388⟧Part II
The processes

The verbs of the theory. Chapter 11 walks through the ten progressions of the web app step by step, with the diagram of every step; chapter 12 lists all 73 processes of the registry, each with its citation and the transcript of iut run on the demo Θ-data (abc(1,2400,2401) l=13).

⟦m389⟧11 · Ten progressions, step by step

Each progression is a sequence of states of the data model; the web app (htdocs/index.html, Part II) lets you step through them with the current Θ-data, and the diagrams below are the same drawings rendered for the demo data. The text under each step is the caption of the web app.

⟦m390⟧11.1 From an abc triple to initial Θ-data

sources [IUT I] Def 3.1 (via [IUTchIV] §2, [Pano] §3) p. 61; [IUT IV] Cor 2.2 p. 41

How the program manufactures the input of the theory: the Frey curve of a + b = c gives E_F over F_mod = Q with multiplicative reduction at the primes of abc; l is chosen; V, V^bad_mod and the fields follow.

step 1 / 6 the triple

Pick coprime positive integers with a + b = c (the generator takes them from the bench above). The height of the triple is log c; the conductor-like quantity is log rad(abc).

step 2 / 6 the Frey curve

The Frey curve turns the additive relation a + b = c into an elliptic curve whose bad primes are exactly the primes of abc. The program records the reduction type and ord_p(q) at each of them.

step 3 / 6 V ≅ V_mod and V^bad_mod

The valuations become the index set of every prime-strip. The odd bad multiplicative primes form V^bad_mod, which must be nonempty — the Θ-link lives there.

step 4 / 6 l, the fields and the labels

The prime l fixes the size of all the label sets (capsules of l and l* prime-strips) and the field K = F(E[l]) whose Galois group must be big. Everything in the data model that is "not computable from integers" (K-core, SL₂ image …) is recorded as an asserted hypothesis.

step 5 / 6 the invariants log q, log f, log d

From the valuations the program computes the quantities that appear in the inequality of [IUTchIII] Cor 3.12 and in the explicit [IUTchIV] Thm 1.10.

step 6 / 6 validate

Every condition of [IUTchI] Def 3.1 that can be checked on numbers is checked; the rest is listed as asserted. The same checks run in the C program (`iut validate`) and in `node htdocs/test.js`.

⟦m391⟧11.2 Forgetting: down the prime-strip ladder

sources [IUT I] Fig I1.2 p. 6, Def 4.1 p. 95, Def 5.2 p. 134; [IUT II] Def 4.9 p. 153; [IUT III] Thm 1.5 p. 48

A prime-strip is built from the Θ-data and then progressively stripped: holomorphic → mono-analytic → units → units mod torsion → only G_v. What survives each step is what the corresponding link can share.

step 1 / 6 F-prime-strip (holomorphic)

Start: the holomorphic Frobenius-like strip, the local data of a Hodge theater. This is the species the log-link needs, since the logarithm uses both ring operations.

step 2 / 6 → F⊢ (forget Π_v)

Forget Π_v, keep G_v: mono-analytic. The splitting O▷ ≅ O▶ × O× becomes part of the data ([IUTchI] Def 5.2 (ii)).

step 3 / 6 → F⊢× (units)

Drop the value groups: only the units O×_v with G_v-action remain.

step 4 / 6 → F⊢×μ (units mod torsion)

Kill the roots of unity: F⊢×μ. This is the strip a Θ-link transports unchanged — the ∧ of the whole theory lives here.

step 5 / 6 → D⊢ (only G_v)

Forget the monoid as well: D⊢, the bi-coric core. Every Hodge theater in the lattice sees the same D⊢ up to Ind1.

step 6 / 6 F⊩▶×μ: what the Θ×μ-links glue

Going back up with global data: the F⊩▶×μ-strips F⊩_Δ, F⊩_env, F⊩_gau, F⊩_LGP, F⊩_lgp are the pilots; the explorer builds all of them at every vertex.

⟦m392⟧11.3 Assembling a Θ±ell NF-Hodge theater

sources [IUT I] Def 4.6 p. 111, Def 5.5 p. 151, Def 6.4 p. 162, Def 6.13 p. 182; [Alien] §3.3 (v) p. 58, §3.6 (ii) p. 87, Fig 3.8 p. 67

One vertex of the lattice is built in five moves: two capsules of prime-strips, four bridges, one gluing. The additive symmetry acts on the left, the multiplicative one on the right.

step 1 / 5 the capsule F_T

A capsule of l F-prime-strips indexed by t ∈ F_l, with distinct basepoints, on which F_l^{⋊±} acts by conjugate synchronization (the ±-symmetry is geometric: it comes from the automorphisms of the elliptic curve).

step 2 / 5 Θ±-bridge and Θell-bridge

The Θ±-bridge collapses the capsule onto a single F-prime-strip F_⊞ (the additive "⊞" label); the Θell-bridge relates the capsule to the D-prime-strip D_⊚± that carries Π_{X_K} and the l-torsion. Together: the Θ±ell-Hodge theater.

step 3 / 5 the capsule F_J

A capsule of l* F-prime-strips indexed by j ∈ F_l^* (the labels |F_l| ∖ {0}), with the multiplicative symmetry F_l^* acting through the number-field side.

step 4 / 5 Θ-bridge and NF-bridge

The Θ-bridge sends the capsule to F_> (the ">" label) inside a Θ-Hodge theater that carries the theta values Θ̲_v(j) = q̲^{j²} and the strips F⊩_tht → F⊩_mod; the NF-bridge relates it to F_⊛ = (Π_{C_K} ↷ F_mod^×), the number-field portion. Together: the ΘNF-Hodge theater.

step 5 / 5 the gluing 0,⊞ ↦ >

Identify the label 0 of F_T with the "⊞" strip and glue the result to F_> via ±j ↦ j: the Θ±ell NF-Hodge theater. Its q-pilot and Θ-pilot are now defined; the capsule F_J will later become the processions S^±_{j+1} of the multiradial representation.

⟦m393⟧11.4 Building the log-theta-lattice (the infinite H)

sources [IUT III] Def 1.1 p. 23, Def 1.4 p. 45, Def 3.8 (iii) p. 112, Thm 1.5 p. 48; [Alien] §3.3 (ii) p. 58, (vi), Fig 3.6 p. 60, Fig 3.15 p. 99; [EssLgc] §3.3 p. 86

The explorer does exactly this when you press l, t and H. Each vertex is a fresh universe; links identify only the parts that are coric.

step 1 / 6 one Hodge theater

Start with one Hodge theater, labelled (0,0) and written †HT. It is a complete copy of the conventional arithmetic geometry of E_F.

step 2 / 6 apply a log-link

The log-link uses the full ring structure, maps units to the additive log-shell of the next vertex, and identifies the étale-like D-prime-strips of domain and codomain ([IUTchIII] Thm 1.5 (i)).

step 3 / 6 iterate: the 0-column

The infinite column is symmetric under vertical shifts; only the whole column, not a finite piece, has this symmetry — which is why the theory needs the "infinite" H.

step 4 / 6 apply the Θ-link

The Θ-link creates the second column. From the point of view of (1,0) the log-links of the 0-column are meaningless: the ring structure that defines them is not transported.

step 5 / 6 the 1-column and the H

The explorer's "build infinite H" button produces exactly this configuration; `iut walk` prints it in text.

step 6 / 6 the whole lattice ⊇ the H

The full lattice is only the ambient bookkeeping. D⊢ (bi-coric), F⊢×μ (horizontally coric) and D (vertically coric) are the three kinds of invariant data ([IUTchIII] Thm 1.5).

⟦m394⟧11.5 The Θ-link: gluing data and alien copies

sources [IUT III] Def 3.8 (ii) p. 112; [IUT II] Cor 4.10 p. 158; [Alien] §3.3 (vii) p. 58, §3.6 (iv) p. 87, Fig 3.19 p. 106

What exactly is identified by the Θ-link (0,0) → (1,0), what is deliberately not, and why the two Hodge theaters are "mutually alien".

step 1 / 6 two Hodge theaters

The Θ-link relates a Θ-pilot to a q-pilot in two independent universes. It is defined only in terms of abstract monoids, which is what makes the gluing possible at all.

step 2 / 6 (aΘ) ≅ (aq): unit group portion

The unit groups modulo torsion, with their Galois actions and integral structures, are glued. This is the horizontally coric F⊢×μ-prime-strip of [IUTchIII] Thm 1.5 (ii).

step 3 / 6 (bΘ) ↦ (bq): local value groups

The theta values on the left are sent to the q-parameter on the right: "q ↦ q^{j²}" averaged over j ([Alien] §2.4). This is where the dilation by l(l+1)/12 — the content of the inequality — enters.

step 4 / 6 (cΘ) ≅ (cq): global realified Frobenioids

The global arithmetic-degree bookkeeping is glued too, so that both pilots have a degree in "the same R" — but only up to the indeterminacies that the chain of ∧'s will track.

step 5 / 6 what is NOT glued

The ring structures, Π_v and everything built with addition stay on their own side. This is the precise meaning of "mutually alien copies": distinct labels that may not be identified ([EssLgc] §3.4, (AOΘ1)–(AOΘ4)).

step 6 / 6 Fig 3.19: the "=" of the Θ-link seen multiradially

The multiradial representation lets the RHS see the LHS's theta values inside its own log-shells: the two sides of the "=" become comparable, at the price of Ind1–3. This is the ∧ of (FxGl) kept alive ([EssLgc] §3.10).

⟦m395⟧11.6 Mono-anabelian transport

sources [Alien] §2.7 p. 21, §2.9 p. 26, Fig 2.1 p. 23; [IUT III] Rem 3.11.1 (APT) p. 159; [AbsTopIII]

The computational technique behind every step of the theory: carry a Frobenius-like object across a link by lifting it to its étale-like container, which the link does preserve, and coming back down.

step 1 / 5 a Frobenius-like object and a link

The question: what does the link do to a Frobenius-like object (e.g. the Θ-pilot)? It cannot be followed through the link as a scheme-theoretic object.

step 2 / 5 Kummer: up to the étale-like container

Kummer isomorphisms lift the object into étale-like data: Galois groups and what can be reconstructed from them by group theory alone.

step 3 / 5 mono-anabelian rigidity across the link

On the étale-like level the link is an isomorphism, and anabelian geometry reconstructs the arithmetic on either side from the group. This is the content of [AbsTopIII] used in IUT.

step 4 / 5 inverse Kummer: back down

The output is the original object re-expressed in the other universe's terms, with the indeterminacies as the price of the detour.

step 5 / 5 the square: an arithmetic change of coordinates

Everything in processes 7 and 10 is an iterate of this square: (Stp1) is the log-Kummer correspondence and Galois evaluation, (Stp2)–(Stp3) are descents to weaker étale-like data.

⟦m396⟧11.7 The chain of logical AND relations: (Stp1)–(Stp8)

sources [EssLgc] §3.6 (∧-Chn) p. 104, (ExtInd), §3.10 (Stp1)–(Stp8) p. 136; [IUT III] Thm 3.11 p. 153, Cor 3.12 p. 173

Mochizuki's own description of the essential logical structure: A ∧ B ⇒ A ∧ (B₁ ∨̇ B₂ ∨̇ …). The ∧ comes from the Θ-link (multiplicative structure common to both sides); the ∨̇'s come from the log-Kummer correspondence (additive structures, not common). The proof never concatenates inequalities; it preserves one ∧.

step 1 / 10 (FxGl): the fixed line segment

Fix the Frobenius-like q-pilot at (1,0) and the gluing, via the Θ-link, of the Frobenius-like Θ-pilot at (0,0) to it. This is the one and only ∧ (simultaneous execution, gluing). Everything that follows adds possibilities (∨̇) to the left end; it never considers two distinct mappings of abstract prime-strips (DstMp) — so there is no commutativity issue (NoCmpIss).

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (FxGl) p. 136, (DstMp), (NoCmpIss); [IUT III] Rem 3.12.2 (ii) p. 187

step 2 / 10 (Stp1) log-Kummer correspondence and Galois evaluation

Exhibit the Frobenius-like Θ-pilot at (0,0) — the data giving the F⊢×μ-prime-strip in the domain of the Θ-link — as one possibility within a collection of possibilities constructed by anabelian algorithms from holomorphic étale-like data of the 0-column. Label descent (0,0) ⇝ (0,◦). Introduces (Ind3), the coarse approximation of the whole log-Kummer apparatus. This is the step that occupies the bulk of [IUTchI–III].

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp1) p. 136, §3.11 p. 152; [IUT III] Thm 3.11 (ii) p. 153, (iii), Rem 3.9.5 (viii) (sQ1) p. 126, (sQ2)

step 3 / 10 (Stp2) introduce (Ind1)

The anabelian algorithms of (Stp1) descend to algorithms needing only the mono-analytic étale-like data, the G_v's: (0,◦) ⇝ (0,◦)⊢. Very mildly enlarges the collection of possibilities by Aut(G_v).

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp2) p. 136; [IUT III] Thm 3.11 (i) p. 153

step 4 / 10 (Stp3) introduce (Ind2): cross the Θ-link

The algorithms descend further to the mono-analytic Frobenius-like data G_v ↷ O×μ (log-shells as submonoids of O×μ rather than subquotients of G_v): (0,◦)⊢ ⇝ (0,0)⊢. Since the Θ-link is an equivalence of labels (0,0)⊢ ⇔ (1,0)⊢ (the full poly-isomorphism of F⊢×μ-strips), the algorithm now has input data (1,0)⊢ from the codomain. This isolates the log-link indeterminacies of the two columns from each other.

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp3) p. 136; [IUT III] Rem 3.9.5 (vii) (Ob7-2) p. 126; [Alien] §3.6 (iv) p. 87

step 5 / 10 (Stp4) holomorphic hull

Pass from the collection of possible regions output by (Stp3) to the regions contained in the holomorphic hull, relative to the 1-column, of their union: a plain application of (ExtInd1), enlarging the set of possibilities (more ∨̇'s).

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp4) p. 136; [IUT III] Rem 3.9.5 (vi) p. 126, (vii) (Ob5)

step 6 / 10 (Stp5) hull-approximants

Replace arbitrary regions in the hull by regions with the same global log-volume that correspond to arithmetic vector bundles. Does not change the ∧/∨ structure, because it does not change the possible value-group portions (the F⊢▶-strips) obtained by taking log-volumes.

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp5) p. 136; [IUT III] Rem 3.9.5 (vii) (Ob6) p. 126

step 7 / 10 (Stp6) tensor power of the determinant

Pass to a suitable positive rational tensor power of the determinant arithmetic line bundle of those vector bundles. Again harmless for the ∧/∨ structure.

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp6) p. 136; [IUT III] Rem 3.9.5 (vii) (Ob3) p. 126, (Ob4)

step 8 / 10 (Stp7) log-shift adjustment: the closed loop

The line bundles of (Stp6) live at the holomorphic structure of (1,1), one log-shift above the codomain (1,0). Applying (Stp1)–(Stp6) at every (1,m) gives diagonal arrows (1,m) → (1,m+1): an endomorphism of the 1-column. Symmetrizing by m ↦ m+1 gives a "closed loop" — a formal, diagram-theoretic gluing between data with distinct labels (1,m)⁺ and (1,m+1)⁻, never a set-theoretic identification. Compatibility with the log-links of the 1-column is obtained by passing to log-volumes, which the log-link preserves.

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp7) p. 136; [IUT III] Rem 3.9.5 (vii) (Ob8) p. 126, (Ob9), (viii) (sQ4)

step 9 / 10 (Stp8) log-volumes and the inequality

Taking log-volumes, the ∧ maintained through (Stp1)–(Stp7) becomes an ∧ between the log-volume of the original q-pilot and the log-volumes of an algorithmically constructed collection of possible outputs, in one copy of R. The inequality of Cor 3.12 is then a formal consequence of the invariance of log-volume under the log-link. The indeterminacies Ind1–3 are the monodromy of the loop, synchronized across all m.

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp8) p. 136; [IUT III] Cor 3.12 p. 173, Rem 3.12.2 (iv) p. 187, (v)

step 10 / 10 summary: ∧(∨̇)-Chn

The ∨̇'s may be read as XOR when the possibilities are listed without overlaps. The passage from Thm 3.11 to Cor 3.12 is then "relatively straightforward", as the word corollary suggests ([EssLgc] §3.6, (Syp1)–(Syp3)).

ref [EssLgc] §3.10 (∧(∨̇)-Chn1)–(Chn4) p. 136, (TrHrc); [EssLgc] §3.6 (∧-Dgns) p. 104

⟦m397⟧11.8 Logical AND versus logical OR

sources [EssLgc] §2.3 Ex 2.3.1–2.3.2 p. 43, §2.4 Ex 2.4.1 p. 46, Ex 2.4.5 p. 50, §3.4 (AOΘ1)–(AOΘ4) p. 94, §3.6 (ExtInd) p. 104

The elementary models from [EssLgc] of what goes wrong when "redundant copies" are identified: a glued pair of segments versus a loop, and a three-line numerical model of the whole theory with sliders.

step 1 / 5 two segments glued at a point: ∧

Ex 2.3.2/2.4.1: †I and ‡I are isomorphic but distinct copies of [0,1], glued at †β = ‡α =: γ_J. Both statements about γ_J hold simultaneously. The coordinate functions x on the two copies glue to a function on J.

ref [EssLgc] Ex 2.3.2 p. 45, Ex 2.4.1 (i) p. 46, Ex 2.4.2 p. 47

step 2 / 5 identify the copies: a loop, ∨ but not ∧

Identify †I with ‡I "because they are redundant": the result is a loop, γ_I is either α or β (∨) but cannot be both (∧ fails). The coordinate function no longer glues — exactly the mechanism of the RCS assertions about IUT (§3.2, §3.4).

ref [EssLgc] Ex 2.4.1 (ii) p. 46, (iii)

step 3 / 5 the numerical model with sliders

Real numbers A, B > 0 and 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 model the Θ-link (the definition N := −2B and the gluing N = −A), the multiradial representation (N = −2A + ε) and the final estimate A = ε ≤ 1. Move the sliders: the ∧'s hold only for A = 2B and ε = A; the point is that nothing forces A = B.

ref [EssLgc] Ex 2.4.5 (i) p. 50, (ii); [Alien] Ex 3.11.4 p. 142

step 4 / 5 the ∨ version: identify A = B

Replace ∧ by ∨ and the distinct numbers look superfluous, so one sets A = B — which makes the original ∧ version of the Θ-link self-contradictory and the passage to the estimate "abrupt, mysterious, unjustified". AND-IUT (the real one) vs OR-IUT / XOR-IUT / RCS-IUT (equivalent) vs EssOR-IUT (accepts the ∧ formally, never uses it).

ref [EssLgc] Ex 2.4.5 (iii)–(vi) p. 50, (XOR/RCS), (EssOR/RCS)

step 5 / 5 (ExtInd): how new ∧'s are made from old

The principle of extension of indeterminacies: the only legitimate way to grow the ∨̇ side without introducing new labels, which is what (sQLTL) — projecting the left column of the H onto the right — requires.

ref [EssLgc] §3.6 (ExtInd) p. 104, (ExtInd1), (ExtInd2), (sQLTL)

⟦m398⟧11.9 The Gaussian-integral analogy

sources [Alien] §1.1 –§1.7 (Steps 1–12) p. 6, §3.8 p. 112, Fig 3.20.1 –3.20.2 p. 113

The "game plan" of IUT explained to a high-school student: a naive substitution is wrong on one copy of the real line, but becomes correct — up to the factor √π — once two mutually independent copies are considered and rotated into each other.

step 1 / 7 the naive substitution fails

The student tries e^{−x²} ⇝ u and gets 1; the infinitesimal dx was not transformed. Partial integrations do not help. This is formally reminiscent of the Θ-link's {q̲^{j²}} ↦ q̲, [IUTchII] Rem 1.12.5.

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (1gau) p. 112

step 2 / 7 two mutually alien copies

Square the integral: consider two identical but independent copies. Nothing clever; the student is indignant. In IUT: the two Hodge theaters in the domain and codomain of the Θ-link, i.e. two copies of the scheme theory around E_F.

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (2gau) p. 112

step 3 / 7 one integral over the plane

The product becomes a single integral over R² — a two-dimensional object, like the lattice, like a ring with its two operations. Integrals are net masses: sums of infinitesimals of zero mass (étale-like containers for positive-mass Frobenius-like objects).

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (3gau) p. 112

step 4 / 7 changes of coordinates

The Jacobian computes the effect of a change of coordinates locally through linear maps: dilations, unipotents, rotations. Mono-anabelian transport is the arithmetic analogue; the MLF examples of §2.12 the analogues of the three linear maps.

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (4gau) p. 112

step 5 / 7 polar coordinates

Rotating the x-copy into the y-copy — passing to polar coordinates — is the analogue of the étale-picture: the two columns become spokes around one coric core, and the multiradial representation is the parallel transport along the rotation.

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (5gau) p. 112

step 6 / 7 decoupling: 1 × π = √π²

Radial and angular parts separate: the radial integral is the naive substitution, now valid; the angular integral is the error factor. In IUT the unit-group and value-group portions decouple by cyclotomic rigidity, the quadratic structure of theta groups playing the role of the quadratic exponent.

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (6gau) p. 112

step 7 / 7 the dictionary

Mochizuki's comparison table ([Alien] Fig 3.20.1–3.20.2).

ref [Alien] §1 p. 6, §3.8 (7gau) p. 112

⟦m399⟧11.10 From the multiradial representation to the log-volume estimate and abc

sources [IUT III] Thm 3.11 p. 153, Cor 3.12 p. 173; [IUT IV] Thm 1.10 p. 22, Cor 2.2 p. 41; [Alien] §3.7 (i)–(iv) p. 103; [ExpEst]

The last ∧ becomes an inequality of real numbers; with explicit constants it is the Szpiro-type bound that implies abc. The numbers below are computed for the current data (a numerical check of the shape of the estimate, not a proof).

step 1 / 6 (∧-Input): an abstract F⊢×μ-prime-strip

The multiradial algorithm asks only for an F⊢×μ-prime-strip, exactly what the Θ-link glues; hence it runs equally on either side.

ref [EssLgc] §3.6 (∧-Input) p. 104; [IUT III] Rem 3.11.1 (ii) p. 159

step 2 / 6 processions of log-shells as containers

The output lives in tensor packets of mono-analytic log-shells indexed by the processions S^±_{j+1} = {0,…,j} (with their (j+1)! permutation symmetries), on which the theta value q̲^{j²} and a copy (F_mod^×)_j act.

ref [Alien] §3.6 (iv) p. 87, (v), Fig 3.16 –3.18 p. 103

step 3 / 6 hull versus Θ-shift, step by step

For each j the container can grow at most by the hull of j+1 log-shells, roughly (j+1) log d^K, while the theta value contributes −(j²/2l) log q. Summing over j = 1..l* and dividing by l* gives the heuristic bound for −|log Θ|.

ref [Alien] §3.7 (iv) p. 103; [IUT IV] Prop 1.4 p. 13

step 4 / 6 Cor 3.12: −|log Θ| ≥ −|log q|

The statement of [IUTchIII] Cor 3.12 and how the current data fares. For small abc triples the hull term dominates and the inequality is comfortably true; it is the explicit constant that carries the content.

ref [IUT III] Cor 3.12 p. 173; [EssLgc] §3.10 (Stp8) p. 136

step 5 / 6 Thm 1.10: the explicit constant

The explicit form of [IUTchIV] Thm 1.10 with the data's numbers. The leading-term heuristic (l²/48)(6 log d^K − log q) of [Alien] §3.7 (iv) is the "size of the inequality" that the multiradial representation produces before normalizing.

ref [IUT IV] Thm 1.10 p. 22, Cor 2.2 p. 41; [ExpEst] ; [Alien] §3.7 (iv) p. 103

step 6 / 6 summary for this data

The whole progression from the integers a + b = c to the inequality, as implemented. Change the data in the bench above and every diagram on this page recomputes.

ref docs/DATA_MODEL.md

ComputeGaussian the Gaussian integral and its IUT analogues ✓ ok

where [Alien] §1 Steps 1-12 p. 6

inputs — outputs √π

    Step  1 the naive approach e^{−x²} ↦ u fails: no elementary antiderivative      —   ↔ a single ring/scheme theory cannot compute the height
    Step  2 partial integration does not help either                              —   ↔ no Frobenius morphism in characteristic 0
    Step  3 introduce a SECOND copy of the integral: I² = ∫∫ e^{−x²−y²}  3.14159   ↔ two mutually alien copies of the ring theory (the two sides of the Θ-link)
    Step  4 regard them as coordinates of R²                                 3.14159   ↔ the log-theta-lattice as a plane of copies
    Step  5 infinitesimals dx dy: the measure                                 3.14159   ↔ log-volumes
    Step  6 the Jacobian: how the measure transforms                          1.00000   ↔ compatibility of log-volumes with the links
    Step  7 linear transformations: toral dilations, unipotent, rotations     1.00000   ↔ the dilation q ↦ q^{j²} of the Θ-link vs the rotation by the log-link
    Step  8 polar coordinates on R² ∖ (R≤0 × {0})                       1.00000   ↔ the coordinates (n, m) of the lattice; the slit = the 'Kummer-detachment' indeterminacy
    Step  9 decoupling of the radial and angular parts                        1.00000   ↔ multiradiality: the radial data is decoupled from the coric data
    Step 10 radial integral ∫_0^∞ e^{−r²} 2r dr = 1                    1.00000   ↔ the multiradial representation computes the Θ-pilot
    Step 11 angular integral ∫_0^{2π} (1/2) dθ = π                       3.14159   ↔ the holomorphic hull / the indeterminacies contribute the constant
    Step 12 √π: the result, with its 'error factor' from the slit          1.77245   ↔ −|log Θ| ≥ −|log q| with the indeterminacies as error term
    numerical ∫e^{−x²} = 1.772454, √π = 1.772454
